reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that same-game parlays require accurate modeling of leg dependencies. Prior to this work, the Gaussian copula used in `run_monte_carlo.py` relied on hand-set illustrative correlations. This primitive estimates those correlations directly from play-by-play data, enabling a true market model. The estimator computes both intra-team (same-side) and inter-team (cross-side) correlations. Cross-side correlations reveal a 'shootout' dynamic where offensive performance rises together, contrary to the intuitive 'clock suppression' hypothesis. These findings are embedded in a structured matrix form suitable for integration into the copula engine. The estimation process corrects prior overconfidence—e.g., the hand-set value of 0.52 for WR-yards ↔ anytime-TD was overstated by 60% compared to the measured 0.3251. This demonstrates the necessity of empirical validation over heuristic assumptions. The resulting matrix enables precise parlay pricing and supports Bayesian inference in GSI and situational reasoning in GSE.
